detection_signals.reasoning: The traffic window shows 39 failed logins across 27 distinct source IPs targeting 8 different usernames within a span of just 1.03 seconds (request rate ~39.8/sec). This high volume of distributed failed login attempts targeting common usernames strongly indicates a credential stuffing or distributed brute force attack.

assessment_at_capture.rationale: The incident shows a coordinated, high-rate distributed credential stuffing attack from known malicious botnet IPs (39.75 req/sec, 40 login attempts, 39 failed logins across 27 distinct IPs within 1.03 seconds). Most importantly, there is 1 successful login recorded amidst the attack, indicating a successful compromise attempt that requires immediate on-call intervention.

correlation.intel_summary: All 5 checked source IPs (203.0.113.13, 203.0.113.36, 203.0.113.47, 203.0.113.40, 203.0.113.41) were identified as 'malicious' with a category of 'botnet', specifically associated with distributed credential-stuffing activity.
correlation.enrichment_notes: The threat intelligence lookup reveals that all 5 top source IPs belong to a known distributed credential-stuffing botnet (203.0.113.0/24). This directly confirms the nature of the attack as automated and coordinated rather than isolated brute-force attempts. Coupled with the high request rate (39.75 req/sec across 29 distinct IPs) and multiple targeted common usernames (guest, root, oracle, etc.), this significantly raises the concern level, confirming a large-scale, automated credential-stuffing campaign.
